brief: BofA raises its CY30E server CPU TAM to $210bn+ from ~$170bn (+36% CAGR vs. +30% prior), reasoning that agentic inference pushes the CPU-to-GPU ratio from ~1:4 in training toward ~1:2 in inference and ~1:1 for agentic AI, as CPUs become the orchestration control plane. This lifts CPUs to about 10% of the ~$2.2Tn CY30 data center systems TAM from about 7% in the CY24-25 training era. BofA frames this as additive, not substitutive: agentic workloads layer new CPU-dense infrastructure alongside GPUs/XPUs, not instead of them. AMD is BofA's top CPU pick on portfolio breadth and dual leadership in frequency and core count (Zen 6 Venice up to 256/512 cores/threads vs. Intel Diamond Rapids 192/192 and Nvidia Vera 88/176). Nvidia remains BofA's top overall sector pick on full-stack leadership, with its Vera CPU rack pushing toward a roughly 1:1 CPU:GPU ratio. Intel gains from foundry optionality and a Q3 supply ramp but BofA sees its value share declining through CY30. ARM is the fastest share gainer, though BofA argues much of that value accrues to licensees like NVDA, with ARM's own AGI CPU reaching meaningful volume only in CY28-30. Qualcomm's CPU visibility is more limited given competition at its key customer.
